messages.content: How do antidepressants work and what are their limitations?

Most common antidepressants: SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) — block reuptake of serotonin, increasing availability in synapse. SNRIs also block noradrenaline reuptake. Simple serotonin-deficit model of depression is oversimplified — evidence is weaker than historically presented. Antidepressants show meaningful benefit over placebo in moderate-severe depression; less clear benefit in mild depression. Limitations: 4-8 week onset, 30-40% don't respond to first medication, side effects (sexual dysfunction, weight gain, discontinuation syndrome), and don't address underlying psychological or social causes. Most effective depression treatment combines medication with psychotherapy.
What is the difference between Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes?

Type 1: autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. No insulin produced. Onset usually childhood/adolescence. Requires exogenous insulin for life. Not preventable with lifestyle changes. Type 2: insulin resistance — cells become less responsive to insulin; pancreas compensates with more insulin; eventually insufficient insulin production. Strongly associated with obesity, physical inactivity, dietary factors, age. Often preventable and sometimes reversible with lifestyle intervention. Treatment: lifestyle change, oral medications (metformin), eventually insulin. The global epidemic is almost entirely Type 2 — driven by diet and activity changes. Type 1 is ~10% of diabetes cases.

Neuroplasticity: the brain's ability to reorganise itself by forming new neural connections throughout life. Not fixed at adulthood. Mechanisms: synaptic plasticity (strengthen or weaken existing connections based on activity), neurogenesis (new neurons in hippocampus — linked to exercise and novel environments), cortical remapping (following injury, adjacent areas can take over functions). Practical implications: skills can be acquired at any age (slower after critical periods but not impossible), recovery from brain injury is possible, mental health conditions (depression, PTSD) involve maladaptive plasticity that can be reversed through therapy and pharmacology.
